apps.name: PoLocalCompare
apps.description: A live arena where two AI models race to build the same web page from one prompt, small open models in your browser on WebGPU against cloud-hosted ones, and the better page wins.

stack.data: Azure Table Storage + Azure Blob Storage

details.frontend: The C# arena, built with Radzen components, shows both generated pages side by side in sandboxed frames and runs the browser contestant's model in a web worker
details.backend: Minimal API groups run duels, tournaments, the model catalog and the leaderboard; background services execute queued duels, resume interrupted tournaments and call the AI judge
details.data: Tables hold duels, results, models, Elo history, tournaments and a daily spend ledger; Azure Blob Storage holds generated pages too large for a table row
details.signIn: Any Microsoft account, work or personal, through a server-side cookie session, so the browser never holds tokens
details.delivery: GitHub Actions builds and deploys every push to Azure; every app except PoTraffic runs its tests there first
details.realtime: One SignalR hub tells your browser when to start its model and streams each side's progress and the final verdict to everyone watching the duel
details.extras: WebLLM runs small open models entirely in your browser on the GPU (WebGPU), downloaded once and cached, racing the cloud models

aiServices.name: GPT-5.4 mini
aiServices.use: Judges every duel unless a person votes within 10 seconds, reading the pages in both orders, and gets the first re-ask when the two orderings disagree

aiServices.name: GPT-5 mini
aiServices.use: Final tie-break when a split survives the re-ask

aiServices.name: AI Foundry contestants
aiServices.use: Sixteen cloud models to pit against each other or the browser models: GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, the GPT-5 family, GPT-4.1 mini, GPT-OSS, Phi-4, Llama 3.3, DeepSeek, Grok, Codestral and Kimi

aiServices.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite
aiServices.use: Reads the second ordering so a verdict must survive a different model family, and also competes

aiServices.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite
aiServices.use: A contestant model from Google

aiServices.name: WebLLM browser models
aiServices.use: Nine small open models (Qwen, Llama, Gemma, SmolLM) that run in your browser on WebGPU

apps.name: PoMiniGames
apps.description: Instant-play browser mini-games, many of them real-time multiplayer: races, brawls, quizzes and board games against friends.

stack.data: Azure Table Storage + Azure Blob Storage

details.frontend: The C# shell hosts about 20 games; most game loops and 3D scenes run in JavaScript modules it loads on demand
details.backend: Minimal APIs serve scores, leaderboards, match history and invites, while server-side game loops run the multiplayer lobbies, races and matches
details.data: Azure Table Storage holds high scores, ladders, Elo ratings, match history and verified results; Azure Blob Storage holds saved PoEcosystem worlds and the keys that sign anti-cheat score tokens
details.signIn: Sign in with a Microsoft account to put your name on leaderboards and play online
details.delivery: GitHub Actions builds and deploys every push to Azure; every app except PoTraffic runs its tests there first
details.realtime: 13 SignalR hubs run lobbies, server-ticked races (up to 50 Hz), lockstep and rollback matches, live quizzes and board games; Web Push delivers game invites
details.extras: three.js draws the 3D games, cannon-es gives them physics, SharpGLTF turns 3D models into destructible voxels on the server and QRCoder makes invite QR codes

apps.name: PoMode
apps.description: Drop in a song and hear what it is made of: stems, pitch, chords and the mode it sits in, plus a Mode Lab that plays each mode over harmony rooted to match.

stack.extras: ONNX Runtime + Whisper.net + AcoustID + DryWetMidi + tus uploads

details.frontend: The C# client, built with Radzen components, plays the stems, draws pitch, chords and beats over the song, records your humming for practice, and can split stems or run a language model in your browser when your device can
details.backend: Minimal APIs take uploads and serve results, while a background worker queue runs each song through separation, pitch, beat, chord, mode and lyrics stages
details.data: Azure Blob Storage mirrors each analysis job's folder, the upload and every result, so jobs survive a restart. No tables
details.signIn: Optional: you start as a guest, and signing in with a Microsoft account keeps your library and lets you open songs from OneDrive
details.delivery: GitHub Actions builds and deploys every push to Azure; every app except PoTraffic runs its tests there first
details.realtime: One SignalR hub pushes each job's progress, server-sent events stream the written interpretation of the song and answers to your questions, and Web Push says when a job finishes
details.extras: ONNX Runtime runs the audio models, Whisper.net transcribes the separated vocals, AcoustID can name the song from its fingerprint, DryWetMidi writes the MIDI export and tus makes big uploads resumable

aiServices.name: GPT-4.1 nano
aiServices.use: Writes the plain-English interpretation of a song and reads free-text Mode Lab requests. The one paid piece, off unless configured

aiServices.name: Whisper.net
aiServices.use: Transcribes the lyrics from the separated vocal on the server

aiServices.name: ONNX audio models
aiServices.use: Split stems (HTDemucs), track notes, vocal pitch, beats and chords, and power sound search (CLAP) on the server

aiServices.name: Browser models
aiServices.use: Chrome's built-in Gemini Nano or a WebLLM model on WebGPU can write the interpretation for free, and a WebGPU vocal model can split stems in the page

apps.name: PoRepoLineTracker
apps.description: Tracks lines of code across all your GitHub repositories over time, so you can point it at an account and watch each repo grow or shrink.

details.frontend: The browser app draws the line-count history, code-health and contributor charts and the repository grids with Radzen components, and installs as a PWA
details.backend: A minimal API queues each repository for analysis in a background worker, serves the history, hotspot, punchcard and year-in-review views, and renders public SVG badges
details.data: Azure Table Storage holds your repositories, the line count for every commit, code-health snapshots and your preferences. No blobs
details.signIn: Sign in with GitHub; the same token lets the app list and clone your repositories
details.realtime: A SignalR hub streams analysis progress only to the repository's owner
details.extras: The git command line clones each repository and walks its history; Roslyn parses C# files for Visual Studio-style code metrics; the GitHub API lists your repositories and registers push webhooks, so new commits are analysed automatically
details.delivery: GitHub Actions builds and deploys every push to Azure; every app except PoTraffic runs its tests there first

apps.name: PoTraffic
apps.description: Measures how unpredictable your commute is, building a baseline from Google Maps travel times for each route and time slot and alerting you when a drive runs long.

stack.extras: Google Maps API + Leaflet maps + Open-Meteo weather

details.frontend: The browser app shows each route on a map, draws travel-time trend charts on a canvas with Radzen controls around them, and installs as a PWA that can receive notifications
details.backend: An API with a Table Storage-backed scheduler that polls each route during your monitoring windows, compares every sample with that route's usual time for the slot, and raises alerts
details.data: Azure Table Storage holds your routes, monitoring windows, every travel-time sample, alerts, push subscriptions and the scheduled jobs. No blobs
details.signIn: Sign in with a Microsoft account
details.realtime: Web Push sends heavier-than-usual, route-changed and time-to-leave alerts plus a Monday digest; routes are polled every 5 minutes, easing to 15 when traffic is steady
details.extras: The Google Maps API supplies live travel times, road shapes, geocoding and address suggestions; Leaflet draws the route on free OpenStreetMap tiles; Open-Meteo adds the weather to each sample, so you can see what rain costs your commute
details.delivery: GitHub Actions builds and deploys every push to Azure; every app except PoTraffic runs its tests there first

apps.name: PoWatch
apps.description: Point a webcam at anything, walk away, and come back to a statistical picture of what happened: motion, objects, regular visitors, time patterns and captions.

stack.data: Azure Table Storage + Azure Blob Storage

details.frontend: The browser app does the watching: it reads the webcam and microphone, runs the detection, captioning and listening models in web workers, and uploads only counts, captions and chosen snapshots
details.backend: An API ingests each session's batches, rolls them into stats, serves recaps and share cards, and runs background jobs for six-hourly data retention and the weekly digest
details.data: Azure Table Storage holds sessions, events, stats rollups, regular visitors, stories and settings; Azure Blob Storage holds the snapshot images and the sign-in encryption keys
details.signIn: Sign in with a Microsoft account
details.realtime: A SignalR hub tells every open tab when new data lands, so the stats pages refresh without polling
details.extras: transformers.js runs object detection, Florence-2 captions, Whisper speech and sound recognition in your browser; QuestPDF renders the session and day recap PDFs
details.delivery: GitHub Actions builds and deploys every push to Azure; every app except PoTraffic runs its tests there first

aiServices.name: GPT-5.4 nano
aiServices.use: Writes session stories and recaps and answers Ask PoWatch questions from your own stats; production uses a built-in template unless switched on

aiServices.name: Gemini Flash-Lite
aiServices.use: The alternative writer for the same recaps and answers

aiServices.name: RF-DETR and Florence-2
aiServices.use: Spot objects and caption what the camera sees, on your device

aiServices.name: Whisper and AudioSet
aiServices.use: Turn speech into words and name sounds like a knock or a dog barking, on your device

apps.name: PoSeeReview

stack.data: Azure Table Storage + Azure Blob Storage
stack.extras: SkiaSharp + Google Places API + MapLibre maps

details.frontend: The browser app finds restaurants near you, pins them on a map, plays each comic with its audio, and shows the generation stream as it arrives
details.backend: An API runs the comic pipeline (score, screen, draw, caption) under daily budgets, plus background jobs that pre-draw popular places, redraw top comics and spot-check image quality
details.data: Azure Table Storage holds restaurants, review analyses, comics, scores, budgets and moderation reports; Azure Blob Storage holds the comic images and their audio
details.signIn: Sign in with a Microsoft account
details.realtime: Comic generation streams its real stages to the page as server-sent events
details.extras: SkiaSharp letters the captions onto the art and builds share cards; the Google Places API finds restaurants and their reviews; MapLibre shows them on free OpenFreeMap tiles

aiServices.name: GPT-5.4 nano
aiServices.use: Reads the restaurant reviews, scores how strange they are and writes the comic's story, captions and scenes; also spot-checks a fifth of the drawn comics

aiServices.name: GPT-5.4 mini
aiServices.use: Writes the audio-comic script and triages moderation reports

aiServices.name: FLUX.1 Kontext pro

aiServices.name: GPT-4o mini TTS

apps.name: PoBox
apps.description: A boxing broadcast where physics-driven boxers with trained brains fight, cameras follow the action and three judges score it.

details.frontend: Built on Unity 6000.6 for the browser in a portrait broadcast layout, with URP renderers tuned separately for phone and PC
details.physics: MuJoCo 3.5, compiled to WebAssembly for the browser, simulates both boxers' bodies at 200 steps a second; the ring has no Unity physics objects at all
details.training: Each boxer learns in stages (footwork, sparring, getting up off the canvas) with the repo's own PPO trainer in PyTorch while MuJoCo Warp runs 4,096 copies of the fight at once on the GPU; every brain is then re-checked in the same MuJoCo 3.5 the game uses
details.extras: Eleven Cinemachine cameras are cut like a TV broadcast, jumping to a close-up just before a heavy punch lands and going overhead for a knockdown count; glTFast imports the eight boxers' 3D models in the editor

aiServices.name: Reinforcement-learning agents
aiServices.use: Each of the eight boxers carries three small neural networks (footwork, fighting and getting up), run by Unity's Inference Engine 50 times a second: each reads 103 numbers about its body and opponent and sets targets for 21 joints

apps.name: PoFootball
apps.description: An AI football sim where trained players run full downs, or you take the snap yourself in QB challenge mode.

details.frontend: A top-down 2D game drawn with URP's 2D Renderer and built for WebGL, so all 22 players play out in the browser
details.physics: Each player is a 2D rigidbody with a circular collider, pushed by forces and capped at a top speed, so blocks and tackles come from real collisions; the ball is moved by game logic, not physics
details.training: Offense and defense are team brains trained with MA-POCA against each other on zero-sum rewards; the quarterback and the defensive play-caller are separate PPO brains, all trained with mlagents 1.1 in Python
details.extras: VContainer wires the game systems together; MessagePipe broadcasts snaps, passes, tackles and scores to the HUD, audio and replays; UniTask runs scene loads and the live-weather lookup; Burst compiles the job that draws the space-control map

aiServices.name: Reinforcement-learning agents
aiServices.use: Four trained brains (offense, defense, quarterback and the defensive play-caller) run in the browser through Unity's Inference Engine; each player sees through 2D ray sensors plus a summary of the ball and field, and the call sheet samples the play-caller brain to show its odds

apps.name: PoHillKing
apps.description: Six physics-simulated human bodies fight to stay on a mountain top as the sea rises, each body type driven by its own trained brain.

details.frontend: Built on Unity 6000.6 for the browser; URP draws the mountain map and the rising sea, and a custom shockwave effect plays on big hits
details.physics: MuJoCo 3.15, compiled to WebAssembly, simulates all six bodies, the hill and the sea's buoyancy at 500 steps a second; Unity's own physics is switched off
details.training: Trained with rsl_rl PPO on PyTorch 2.9 while MuJoCo Warp runs 4,096 hilltop fights at once on the GPU; each body's fighter learned against the other two bodies' frozen fighters
details.extras: Cinemachine is the only camera: a crane shot up the mountain on a spline for the intro, then orbits and group shots of whoever is still on top, with shake on big impacts; glTFast imports Trump's model and the mountain map in the editor

aiServices.name: Reinforcement-learning agents
aiServices.use: Kim, Trump and Grandpa each have a fighter brain and a get-up brain that Unity's Inference Engine runs 50 times a second, reading 112 numbers about the body and its nearest opponent and driving 29 joints; the training critics also power the live win-odds bar

apps.name: PoOlympic
apps.description: Up to eight physics-simulated athletes, driven by trained brains, compete in made-up Olympic-style events such as Sumo Ring, Narrow Bridge and Hilltop Scramble.

details.frontend: Built on Unity 6000.6 for the browser as a portrait sports broadcast, with URP drawing the stadium and 13 event arenas
details.physics: MuJoCo 3.11, compiled to WebAssembly, simulates up to eight athletes plus the event props and obstacles at 200 steps a second
details.training: Trained with mjlab on MuJoCo Warp and rsl_rl PPO in PyTorch, one skill at a time (standing, running, crawling, slopes, getting up) for each of the four bodies, then checked against the game's MuJoCo before shipping
details.extras: Cinemachine cuts follow the race's tension, closing in on the leader or on an athlete about to fall; glTFast imports the athletes and stadium in the editor; VFX Graph makes the impact sparks on Android, while the web build swaps in ordinary particles; PrimeTween animates the scoreboard captions

aiServices.name: Reinforcement-learning agents
aiServices.use: About 27 small skill brains (stand, run, crawl, climb slopes, get up) for four athletes run in Unity's Inference Engine 50 times a second; each reads 84 numbers about its body and a speed command, and sets targets for 23 joints

apps.name: PoRace
apps.description: A Unitree Go2 robot dog and humanoid racers run on MuJoCo physics, with every stride coming from a trained locomotion policy.

stack.extras: Unitree Go2 and G1 models + Open-Meteo weather

details.frontend: Unity 6000.6 built for WebGL and drawn with URP; Unity's own physics is never used, it only runs the cameras, the broadcast HUD and the replays. The Unity source now lives in the PoRaceUnreal repo, which is rebuilding the game in Unreal
details.physics: Every racer and the track run in one MuJoCo model inside the browser, stepping every 4 ms (250 times a second) through MuJoCo's Unity plugin
details.training: Trained on a GPU in a Docker trainer with MuJoCo Playground and Brax PPO in JAX: the Go2 learned to run, take banked and steeplechase tracks and get up, and the humanoids use Playground's G1 walking setup
details.extras: Blue is a model of the Unitree Go2 robot dog and the humanoid racers use the Unitree G1's 29-joint layout; a race can pull a real city's current weather from Open-Meteo to change grip and wind

aiServices.name: Reinforcement-learning agents
aiServices.use: Every stride is a trained ONNX policy that Unity's Inference Engine runs 50 times a second in the browser; it reads the racer's joints, body motion and steering command (48 numbers for the Go2) and sets its motor targets

apps.name: PoSoccer
apps.description: Top-down pocket soccer played between players trained with Unity ML-Agents.

details.frontend: A top-down 2D pitch drawn with URP's 2D Renderer and built for WebGL for portrait play in the browser
details.physics: Each player and the ball are 2D rigidbodies and all ball control is physical contact: heavier players win collisions, and a hard hit briefly costs a player control
details.training: Each character has its own PPO brain and reward table, trained in stages against a rule-based bot, with a curriculum that narrows the goal and toughens the bot; trained with an embedded copy of ML-Agents 4.1
details.extras: UniTask times the kickoff countdown, halftime and hit effects; 2D Tilemap builds the crowd stands around the pitch at runtime

aiServices.name: Reinforcement-learning agents
aiServices.use: Ten trained character brains run in the browser through Unity's Inference Engine; each sees the ball, opponents and walls through separate 2D ray sensors plus a short history of its own state, and outputs drive, strafe, turn and boost

apps.name: PoSumo
apps.description: Trained ragdoll wrestlers try to push each other out of a shrinking sumo ring.

details.frontend: A side-on 2D arena drawn with URP's 2D Renderer and built for WebGL, so bouts play in the browser
details.physics: Each wrestler is a 14-part 2D ragdoll held together by motorised hinge joints whose strength drops with speed like real muscle, so every shove, grip and stumble is simulated
details.training: Each wrestler has its own PPO brain trained by self-play against past versions of itself, with the ring width, starting gap and shrinking ring randomised between rounds
details.extras: ML-Agents is built from a patched copy of its source kept in the repo; Timeline sequences the opening and promotion ceremonies

aiServices.name: Reinforcement-learning agents
aiServices.use: Sixteen trained wrestler brains run in the browser through Unity's Inference Engine; each reads 51 body and contact measurements, mirrored so one brain works facing either way, and drives the ragdoll's joint motors

apps.name: PoSlapUnreal
apps.description: A slap-fight arena built in Unreal Engine whose fighters are trained with reinforcement learning; watch them fight in the browser.

stack.extras: Unreal Robotics Lab + NNE (ONNX Runtime) + three.js + Pixel Streaming 2

details.frontend: The full game is Unreal Engine 5.8, which only draws the slappers while its Chaos physics is switched off on everything; the website is a separate three.js version of the same match that runs MuJoCo's WebAssembly build in the browser
details.physics: MuJoCo 3.10 steps both fighters' bodies, the arena and every slap contact 200 times a second, with the same physics in the trainer, the Unreal game and the browser
details.training: Each character climbs a ladder of levels on the GPU (walk in, stand, hold guard, land a slap, absorb one, then a self-play duel and a full-match exam) while PyTorch PPO learns a policy that reads about 140 numbers and moves 30 joints
details.extras: Unreal Robotics Lab runs MuJoCo inside Unreal and NNE runs each fighter's ONNX brain on the CPU 50 times a second; the browser runs the same brains with ONNX Runtime Web and draws them with three.js; Pixel Streaming 2 is only a local script that streams an Unreal match to phones on the same network

aiServices.name: Reinforcement-learning agents
aiServices.use: Each fighter is a trained ONNX brain that picks joint targets 50 times a second: Unreal's NNE runs it in the game, and ONNX Runtime Web runs it on the website, where you predict who lands the next slap

apps.name: PoFightJudge
apps.description: Pick two personas and a topic and watch them argue it out in synthesised voices, or argue it yourselves live with an AI host, while an AI judge scores and fact-checks the fight.

stack.data: Azure Table Storage + Azure Blob Storage

details.frontend: The C# client, built with Radzen components, runs the debate stage, plays the voices with animated effects and captures your microphone for spoken turns
details.backend: Minimal API modules (Carter) start and end fights and serve profiles, history and the leaderboard, while background workers transcribe, judge and fact-check finished fights
details.data: Nine tables hold profiles, matches, turns, analyses, results and share links; Azure Blob Storage holds the recorded fight audio, profile faces and cached speech
details.signIn: Sign in with a Microsoft account; your fights, history and profile are tied to it
details.delivery: GitHub Actions builds and deploys every push to Azure; every app except PoTraffic runs its tests there first
details.realtime: One SignalR hub, using MessagePack, carries raw microphone audio up and the host's voice, captions and snapshots down; the server talks to the GPT-Realtime host over its own WebSocket
details.extras: Concentus compresses each recorded fight to Opus before it is stored; transformers.js can transcribe a spoken turn in your browser; MessagePack keeps the audio-heavy SignalR traffic compact

aiServices.name: Whisper tiny

details.backend: An API queues each run's steps in a background dispatcher, calls the image, video, music and speech models, renders video, and deletes media after 30 days
